text:
Sean Walker went undrafted, came up through Bowling Green and the AHL, and is now a Stanley Cup champion in his second year in Carolina. At 32 he is having one of the better scoring months of his career, and he scored in what CBS Sports called a milestone appearance, at Madison Square Garden.

Six points in his last ten games, four of them goals, against an expected four or so. Our numbers call it mostly earned: he is generating more of his own chances than usual, even if 9.1% shooting from the blue line is running hot next to our range of 4.8 to 7.9.

The real value is the stuff that doesn't show up in the points column. Carolina takes 62% of the 5v5 shot attempts with him on the ice, he has 48 blocks, and Evolving-Hockey had him 52nd of 215 defensemen by wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength defense. The caveat from the same source: he plays with very strong teammates, which flatters any Hurricane's raw numbers. Walker's job is to keep a machine running, and he is doing it.
headline: Sean Walker, still doing the quiet work
